elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If shock/SBP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until SBP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
COLLAPSE/FALLS

Approach to the patient who has collapsed not needing urgent attention • Do an ECG. If abnormal, refer same day. • Check Hb: if < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely 44. • Screen for substance use. In the past year, has patient drunk ≥ 4 drinks3/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription/over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165. • Check BP: if ≥ 140/90 148. Then measure BP after lying for 5 minutes and repeat again after standing for 3 minutes. Does systolic BP drop by ≥ 20 or diastolic BP drop by ≥ 10?
Was patient breathing very quickly or deeply immediately before or during the collapse?
Yes

Hyperventilation likely • May also have light- headedness, chest tightness, tingling of hands/feet and visual changes. Usually with emotional stress. • Reassure and encourage to breathe at normal rate. • Assess for stress and anxiety 98.
Did patient have dizziness, light-headedness, nausea, sweating,
weakness or vision changes before the collapse?
Yes
Common faint likely • Advise to avoid triggers like overheating, dehydration and prolonged standing. • Advise to lie flat with legs raised as soon as symptoms occur.
• If collapse associated with coughing, swallowing, head turning, refer. • If known diabetes 145.

• If none of the above, look for and manage likely cause: if vision problems 48, joint problems 77, foot problems 81, leg problems 80, dementia 166. • Refer if patient > 65 years with possible heart disease, patient collapses/falls repeatedly or cause for collapse/falls is uncertain.
Yes

Orthostatic hypotension likely • Common in the elderly. • Review medications: e.g. fluoxetine, amitriptyline, amlodipine, enalapril, furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, isosorbide dinitrate can cause collapse/falls. Discuss with doctor. • If diarrhoea 58, if vomiting 57, if fever 38. If poor fluid intake, encourage fluids, give oral rehydration solution. • Advise patient to sit first before standing up from lying down. • Refer if: - Diabetes - Peripheral neuropathy (pain/numbness of feet) - Tremor, slow movements or stiffness - History of constipation or erection problems

1Common allergens: medication, food or insect bite/sting within the past few hours. 2If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 3One drink is 1 tot of spirits, or 1 small glass (125mL) of wine or 1 can/ bottle (330mL) of beer.
